description: The observer in `$.last-token.source-text = "b"` reads the original input through the span projection. The chosen a elides T at 0 and at 2, so the reconstructed input is T A B T, and c reads both synthetic T as bare terminals. a survives only if $.last-token is the original B token; then a and c are two readings. Read over the reconstructed tokens, $.last-token is the trailing synthetic, whose text is empty, a is lost, and c alone would pass (engine §7.5).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%rule text a | b | c
%rule a ([+T="ta"] $x:pair [+T="ta"]) %conditions $.last-token.source-text = "b"

%rule b ([+T="ta"] [+T="ta"] pair [+T="ta"])
%rule c (T="ta" pair T="ta")
%rule pair (A B)
%rule term T
